meta.description: Design an organic, irregular mirror on a photo of your wall and export a free 1:1 printable cutting template across ordinary paper. Runs entirely in your browser.

exact.body: Every sheet carries registration marks, overlap guides and a 10 cm ruler so you can confirm the scale before you cut.

templates.body: Organic waves, pebbles, pills and more — or draw your own by dragging smooth control points.

how.title: Four steps to a mirror that fits your wall
how.intro: The whole thing is grounded in real centimeters, so what you print is what you cut — no guesswork, no scaling surprises.

s1.title: Photograph the wall
s1.body: Snap the spot where the mirror will hang. Any phone photo works.

s2.title: Calibrate the scale
s2.body: Mark a rectangle you know the real size of and type it in centimeters. The photo is straightened to a head-on view at true scale.

s3.title: Design the shape
s3.body: Start from {{count}} templates, then drag the curve, move and scale it until it sits exactly right on your wall.

s4.title: Print at 1:1
s4.body: Export a full-size PDF tiled across A4, A3 or Letter. Print at 100%, tape the sheets, trace the outline.

q1.q: How do I print a template at exactly 1:1 scale?
q1.a: In the print dialog turn off “fit to page” / “shrink oversized pages” and set the scale to 100%. Page 1 carries a 10 cm ruler — measure it with a real ruler before you cut anything. If it measures 10 cm, every other sheet is right too.

q2.q: Can I make an irregular or asymmetrical shape?
q2.a: Yes — that is the point. Start from one of the {{count}} templates, then drag any control point, double-click the outline to add one, or delete points you don’t want. Nothing is constrained to a symmetry axis.

q3.q: What paper sizes can I use?
q3.a: A4, Letter, A3, Legal and A2, in portrait. The page count updates as you switch, so you can trade sheet size against how many pages you tape together. Sheets overlap by 10 mm with registration crosses to align on.

q4.q: How do I get the glass cut from the template?
q4.a: Tape the printed sheets into one full-size stencil, cut along the outline, and hand that paper shape to a glazier — it is the physical pattern they work from. The finished size is printed on page 1 so you can quote the job without re-measuring.

q5.q: Does my photo get uploaded anywhere?
q5.a: No. Everything runs in your browser — the photo, the calibration and the PDF are all generated on your own device and stored only there. There is no account and no server to upload to.

closing.title: Ready to fit a mirror to your wall?
closing.body: Design it in minutes and walk away with a template you can cut to.

calibrate.dropBody: Choose a photo of the wall where the mirror will go.
calibrate.hintTitle: Place the rectangle inside the area you want to mirror.
calibrate.hintSub: Drag the 4 corners onto a real rectangle on the wall — or drag from the middle to move the whole rectangle — and type its true size. On Done, the photo is straightened so you design on a head-on wall.
calibrate.panelHint: Type the real-world size of the rectangle you drew. This grounds the whole design in centimeters.
calibrate.quadInvalid: Fix the corners — the rectangle must be a proper (convex) shape.
calibrate.errImage: Could not read that image. Please choose a different photo.
calibrate.errFile: Could not read that file. Please choose a different photo.

editor.canvasAria: Mirror shape editor: drag the outline or its control points

catalog.title: Choose a mirror
catalog.infoBody: Pick a shape, then drag the dots on the canvas to refine it. Double-tap the outline to add a point; select one and use the Delete point button (or the Delete key) to remove it.

print.title: Print your 1:1 template
print.sub: Your mirror is {{size}}. Choose a paper size — it prints across multiple sheets you tape together.
print.noArea: Shape has no area to print.
print.error: Could not build the PDF. Check your connection and try again.
print.fineprint: Print at 100% — turn off “fit to page”. Page 1 has a 10 cm ruler to check scale.
print.watermarkLabel: Add a QR to {{app}} inside the printed mirror
print.watermarkSub: So anyone who sees your template can find the app. Also stamps the app name on downloaded images.
print.pdfLanguageNote: The PDF itself is in English.
